title: API contracts, response envelopes and client-version compatibility are inconsistent

original_titles.title: Success response envelope {data, meta{request_id, server_time}} not implemented on any endpoint
server_time is not carried on every response
server_time not carried on responses; timestamps serialized with +00:00 instead of Z
No machine-checkable API contract (no openapi.yaml, errors.yaml, schemas, copy catalog)
Hand-written API client; no OpenAPI generation, no runtime schema validation, no X-Min-Client-Version
Error catalog code/status mismatches and missing canonical codes (DRAFT_VERSION_CONFLICT 412 not 409; 413 returns SUBMISSION_INVALID)
Draft optimistic concurrency uses body version instead of If-Match; DRAFT_VERSION_CONFLICT is 412 not 409
Copy catalog / copy_key in meta absent; error messages hardcoded
API client is hand-written; no OpenAPI generation or staleness check
Unknown error code silently degrades to HTTP 400 instead of failing loudly

problem: The API returns hand-built endpoint-specific success shapes; server_time is present only on selected auth/state endpoints. The frontend client is handwritten without generated/runtime request/response validation or a minimum-client-version gate. The error catalog also contains known status/contract deviations such as DRAFT_VERSION_CONFLICT using 412 and body-size 413 mapping to SUBMISSION_INVALID.
impact: Frontend/backend contract drift is detected late, older clients can continue using incompatible payloads, and consumers cannot rely on a stable success envelope or clock-sync metadata.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Export a canonical OpenAPI document from the FastAPI app and validate it in CI. Add explicit Pydantic models for every request/response instead of dict bodies and manual casts.
Generate TypeScript client/types from OpenAPI or use runtime schemas (for example Zod) at the API boundary. Fail CI when generated types are stale.
Choose one success response convention and migrate clients incrementally; include request_id and server_time where timing/diagnostics require it. Document intentional legacy responses.
Add X-Min-Client-Version or a config capability response and return 426 CLIENT_TOO_OLD with a safe reload path when a client is unsupported.
Normalize error code/status mapping, pagination fields and optimistic-concurrency semantics; include contract tests for every public route.

acceptance_criteria: OpenAPI generation and validation runs in CI.
All errors use documented code/status pairs.
Client version policy rejects unsupported clients before mutation.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
